blogs.title: The Patient Who Forgot to Breathe: Acquired Ondine's Curse and Chiari I
blogs.description: This post explores the terrifying phenomenon of 'automatic' vs. 'voluntary' respiratory drive. We'll analyze the case of a patient with Chiari Malformation Type I (CMI) who experienced profound, asymptomatic oxygen desaturations, mimicking Congenital Central Hypoventilation Syndrome. We'll discuss the pathophysiology of brainstem compression, the absence of dyspnea during hypoxia (loss of interoception), and why some patients can 'forget to breathe' despite having a preserved conscious drive to ventilate.

blogs.title: Beyond the Endoscope: When 'Normal' Swallowing Studies Mask Brainstem Pathology
blogs.description: When a patient presents with recurrent choking but has normal laryngoscopies and endoscopies, where do you look next? This post discusses the distinction between mechanical and neurogenic dysphagia, highlighting how CMI can cause oropharyngeal dysfunction via lower cranial nerve nuclei compression. We'll discuss the clinical 'red flag' of equal difficulty with both solids and liquids and why structural brain imaging should be considered in unexplained bulbar symptoms.

blogs.title: The Danger of the 'Normal' Report: Re-evaluating Old Imaging in Chronic Cases
blogs.description: A 'normal' radiology report is a snapshot in time, not an absolute truth. This post examines the diagnostic pitfall of relying on a 14-year-old CT report that missed a 'crowded foramen magnum.' We'll discuss the importance of retrospective image review in complex cases, the role of trauma in unmasking congenital variants, and how a unified diagnosis can emerge from revisiting the earliest pieces of a patient's medical history.

blogs.title: AHI vs. Reality: The Pitfalls of Type III Sleep Studies in Central Apnea
blogs.description: Is a low Apnea-Hypopnea Index (AHI) always reassuring? We dive into the technical limitations of Type III home sleep testing versus Type I polysomnography. Using this case, we explain why the lack of EEG monitoring can lead to a significant underestimation of central apnea severity and why clinicians should be skeptical of 'mild' results when the patient's clinical presentation (e.g., nocturnal choking and profound desaturation) suggests a more severe pathology.

blogs.title: Vertex Pain and Hair-Cutting: Recognizing Atypical Presentations of Chiari Syndrome
blogs.description: While occipital headaches are the hallmark of Chiari I, this case presents a bizarre clinical pearl: vertex allodynia relieved by cutting one's hair. We'll discuss the intersection of structural brain abnormalities and scalp hypersensitivity, exploring the concepts of 'burning vertex syndrome' and occipital neuralgia, and how atypical pain patterns can serve as a clue to underlying posterior fossa decompression needs.
